text:
incident-bot: PAGER: prod-west serving cluster reports spike in CUDA OOMs and node flaps across svc-infer-pool-7. Severity: high. Pager: @sre-oncall. Link: https://internal.incidents/3122223334

alice: seeing repeated OOMs and container restarts on node gpu-w-14 and gpu-w-15. logs show CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS then container terminated.

miguel: noticing coincident IB retransmit errors in dmesg around same time. possible RDMA layer timeouts -> KV cache thrash?

alice: exact log snippets:
```
[2026-03-15T02:45:12Z] cuda: kernel failed: CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS
[2026-03-15T02:45:12Z] containerd: killing container svc-infer-abc (exit code 134)
[2026-03-15T02:45:12Z] runtime: oom killer invoked on pid 2456
```

eng-runtime: also pulled infra-net logs: `mlx5_core`: "REQ timed out" and multiple `IB RX completion errors` on mlx5_0.

infra-pager: from the NIC side we see increased retransmits and path down notifications on rack-7 TORs at ~02:43Z. Might be microburst / ECN reaction.

sre-oncall: impact check — are customers getting 5xx or just elevated latency?

support: we have customers in chat reporting 502/504 on generation endpoints; timestamps match 02:44-02:47Z and some report degraded token throughput.

kevin: quick mitigation suggestion: shift routing for impacted service to prod-east fallback pool and reduce max_concurrency to 1 for affected model to avoid memory spikes.

pm-olivia: need statement for affected customers — lowest impact tier customers first? Which customers hit hardest?

alice: quick try: disabling cross-node KV cache on cluster to avoid RDMA traffic for KV lookups. Command (rolling):
```
# disable kvcache via runtime flag
kubectl -n infra set env ds/serving-runtime KVCACHE_MODE=local
# then gracefully restart pods on gpu-w-14,gpu-w-15
kubectl drain gpu-w-14 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl rollout restart deploy/svc-infer-pool-7
```

miguel: note that disabling kvcache increases load on compute and mem per process. doing this while OOMs are occuring is risky — do a canary on a single node first.

alice: canary done on gpu-w-16, no OOMs for ~3min, but latency up 30%.

eng-runtime: pushing routing change to divert 30% of traffic to prod-east now:
```
curl -X POST https://control-plane.local/traffic_shift -d '{"service":"svc-infer","from":"prod-west","to":"prod-east","pct":30}'
```

incident-bot: NOTE: runbooks triggered: serving-ooms, rdma-fabric-degrade.

infra-pager: NVidia driver stack shows occasional `GPU reset detected` messages concurrent with IB errors; possible PCIe interrupts due to NIC driver. Opening ticket with NIC vendor.

sre-oncall: short customer impact summary for ops channel: "Partial service degradation in prod-west between 02:43-03:02Z causing elevated latencies and intermittent 5xx for some customers. Traffic partially shifted to prod-east and affected nodes drained. No data loss. Investigation points to RDMA fabric retransmits causing KV cache thrash -> OOMs and container restarts."

support: sending targeted notifications to customers impacted 1,3,7 — drafting now.

kevin: further mitigation: reduce model batch size and set batch_timeout=5ms for the pool to reduce mem pressure:
```
PATCH /api/v1/pools/svc-infer-pool-7/config
{
  "batch_size": 1,
  "batch_timeout_ms": 5
}
```

alice: applied batch config on canary then rolled to remainder. OOM rate dropped by ~80% but latency increased.

miguel: running `ibdiagnet` and `ib_read_bw` tests on rack-7 during quieter window to reproduce; captured packet counters showing sustained retransmit burst ~02:42-02:48Z.

eng-runtime: made temporary policy change: route fallback to CPU-quantized model for non-SLA customers to reduce GPU churn. command:
```
POST /admin/rollout
{"service":"svc-infer","route":"fallback-cpu-q","pct":50}
```

pm-olivia: thanks — support message ready. Also want a short external note: "We experienced partial serving degradation in us-west; we shifted workload and applied mitigations; investigating root cause. Will follow up within 2 hours."

infra-pager: NIC vendor confirmed driver telemetry shows firmware-level heartbeat warnings coincident with our errors. They recommended temporary port flap dampening and qlen tuning on switches. Scheduling config change with network team.

sre-oncall: for postmortem — action items: 1) collect full dmesg + kernel logs from affected nodes, 2) packet captures on TORs, 3) evaluate KVCACHE fallback behaviour under retransmit, 4) vendor firmware escalation, 5) consider automatic traffic shift policy when OOM + IB errors co-occur.

kevin: assigning follow-ups: infra to own NIC vendor ticket (infra-12345), eng-runtime to prepare test harness to simulate IB retransmit -> kvcache thrash, support to finalize customer comms, PM to draft external note.

alice: final status at 03:00Z: draining complete for gpu-w-14/gpu-w-15, retransmits subsided, OOMs stopped after config changes and traffic shifts. Keeping cluster at reduced concurrency for next 2 hours.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigations applied and partial recovery observed. Owners: infra, eng-runtime. Postmortem pending.

pm-olivia: will schedule postmortem meeting 10am PT and include customers who were impacted.

support: closing customer tickets as fixed where applicable, leaving proactive note.

kevin: leaving a note in runbook: "If RDMA retransmit + OOM coincide, immediately: 1) shift traffic regionally, 2) disable kvcache canary, 3) reduce batch sizes, 4) alert NIC vendor."

sre-oncall: handing off to daytime oncall (miguel) for monitoring and next steps.

miguel: ack. monitoring alerts suppressed for known false positives; will follow up with full postmortem.
